core_claim.quote: These convergent findings indicate that conscious access is not attached to early sensory processing but instead relates to a late stage whose timing is often decoupled from the timing of the actual stimulus.

source.citation: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux J-P, Dehaene S. Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis. Neuron 105(5):776-798, 2020

prediction.statement: The first 200 ms or so of processing can be the same whether or not a stimulus becomes conscious; the difference starts later.

first_stated.passage: In EEG, MEG, and intracranial recordings, conscious stimuli, compared to matched non-conscious ones, induce a late (~300 ms) and sudden increase in slow event-related potentials

source.citation: Dehaene S, Charles L, King J-R, Marti S. Toward a computational theory of conscious processing. Current Opinion in Neurobiology 25:76-84, 2014

prediction.test_for: With stimulus and task matched, the earliest reliable difference between consciously perceived and unperceived stimuli appears after about 200 ms.
prediction.test_against: With stimulus and task matched, a reliable awareness-related difference appears before 200 ms and carries the conscious content.

other_statements_of_the_prediction.passage: The first 200 ms of brain activity, corresponding to early perceptual processing, can be fully preserved on trials without conscious perception, particularly under inattention conditions
